hero.h1: Report a claim.We’ll do it with you.
hero.lede:
Enter your policy number and we’ll show you your company’s claims line.
        Or skip it — call us and a licensed agent files it with you, start to finish.

now.b: If anyone is hurt, call 911 first.
now.p:
Insurance can wait fifteen minutes. Nothing on this page is more urgent than
            that call, and no carrier will hold it against you that you rang them second.

form.label: Policy number
form.hint:
Stays in your browser — nothing is sent or saved.
          Spaces and dashes don’t matter. Don’t have it? The list below is by company name.

dir.sub:
Every company we place business with, and the line that takes a new
      claim. Calling is usually faster than a form — they will ask questions no form
      thinks to ask.
dir.note: Not sure which one is yours? Call 915-503-1207 or text 915-594-3777. We hold your policy on our side, so we can tell you the company and the claim number in about a minute — and we can make the report with you on the line if you would rather not do it alone.

scene.h3: What to do before you leave the scene

photos.b: Photograph more than you think you need
photos.p:
Both cars from four corners, both plates, the damage close up, the whole
          intersection, the street signs, the road surface. Photos taken later cannot be
          taken at all.

card.b: Get the other driver’s insurance card
card.p:
Company name, policy number, name on the policy, plate, and their phone.
          Photograph the card rather than writing it down. Do not discuss whose fault
          it was — that is not decided at the scene.

report.p:
In Texas and New Mexico, officers give you a card or a case number before they
          leave. Carriers ask for it on the first call, and chasing it afterwards costs
          days.

warn.b: Report it even if you are not sure you want to claim.
warn.p1:
Reporting and claiming are two different things. Telling your carrier what
         happened is usually required by the policy itself, and it does not commit you to
         filing. What does cause trouble is a carrier hearing about a crash weeks later
         from the other driver’s insurer instead of from you — that is when a claim gets
         hard to pay.
warn.p2:
If the damage looks smaller than your deductible and nobody else was involved,
         call us before you decide. It takes one conversation to work out whether a claim
         is worth making.

who.q: Should I call you or the insurance company?
who.a:
Either works, and there is no penalty for calling us first. We are your agent,
          not your insurer — the carrier decides and pays the claim, and we make sure it
          is reported correctly, chase it when it goes quiet, and translate what they tell
          you. A lot of people find that easier than starting alone.

when.q: How long do I have to report it?
when.a:
Policies say "promptly" rather than a number of days, which sounds vague and is
          not: the clock that matters is how long the evidence lasts. Report it the same
          day if you can. Late reporting is one of the few things that can genuinely cost
          you a claim.

rate.a:
It depends on fault, on your record, and on the carrier — and it can go up
          after a not-at-fault claim with some companies and not with others. Nobody can
          promise you either way before the claim is decided. What we can do is re-shop
          your policy at renewal if it does move.

ded.q: What is my deductible and when do I pay it?
ded.a:
It is on your declarations page, usually $500 or $1,000, and it comes out of
          what the carrier pays for your own car — you never write us a cheque for it.
          If the other driver is found at fault, you can often get it back. Call and we
          will read your page with you.

rental.q: Do I get a rental car?
rental.a:
Only if the policy carries rental coverage, and only for a covered claim. It is
          a separate coverage, it has a daily limit, and plenty of people find out they do
          not have it on the day they need it. Ask us and we will tell you what is on your
          policy right now.

fault.q: The other driver was at fault. Do I still call mine?
fault.a: Yes. You can claim against their insurer instead, and sometimes that is the right move — but tell yours what happened anyway. If the other carrier disputes fault or the driver turns out to be uninsured, you are going to need your own policy, and it is much easier when they already know. How a claim actually works →

card.s: We can send a copy by text or email

pay.s: Straight to your carrier’s payment page

less.b: See if you can pay less

learn.b: How a car insurance claim actually works
learn.d:
Who decides fault, what a deductible really costs you, how long
          each step takes, what a total loss means, and the mistakes that make a claim
          harder than it needed to be.

miss.body: Only some companies number their policies in a way we can read, and a typo looks the same as an unknown one. Find your company in the list below, or call us the number and we will tell you who wrote it — it takes seconds.
